final_prompt:
I'm preparing a kickoff for engineering and design leads on a B2B note-taking app. The decision they make at the kickoff is whether to commit to building team workspaces, and what v1 includes. Write the PRD they will read. It is a draft for me to edit.

Problem and evidence: the problem is only known as "the app needs team workspaces". I have no evidence to share right now (no data, no customer quotes). In the Problem section, state the problem in one or two plain sentences based only on what I've said here. Then add a clearly marked "Evidence gap" note saying that evidence is still to be gathered. Do not invent customer quotes, statistics, or research.

Scope for v1
In:
- Create a workspace.
- Invite members by email.
- Shared notes inside a workspace.
- Two roles only: admin and member.

Out (list these under non-goals and scope-out):
- Billing changes.
- SSO.
- Guest access.

Open question to keep open: what happens to existing shared notes when workspaces launch (migration). Describe the question and the options you see, but do not recommend or decide.

Everything else (permissions detail, notifications, limits, and so on): I have no preference. Either list it under Open questions for engineering and design to settle, or leave it out. Do not turn guesses into requirements.

Success metric: 20% of paid accounts create a workspace within 60 days of launch. This is my target, so state it as given. Do not add other numeric targets. If you think a supporting metric is useful, name it without a number and label it "proposed".

Sections, in this order: Overview, Problem (with the evidence gap marked), Goals and non-goals, Users, Requirements, Scope in/out, Success metric, Open questions, Risks. For Users, use only the two roles above plus the buying and admin context a B2B app implies. For Risks, include the missing evidence and the migration question, plus any others you can reasonably infer. Label inferred risks as inferred.

Length: at most about 2 pages. Write for readers who will act on it: concrete requirements, short sentences, no filler. Use headings and short bullet lists for requirements.

At the end of the doc, add a short "Assumptions" list naming anything you had to assume. If you assumed nothing, write "None". Reply with the PRD and the Assumptions list only. Nothing follows them.
